title: Coherent microwave-to-optical transduction with Yb:YSO spins strongly coupled to a 3D resonator
authors: Ujjwal Gautam, Nasser Gohari Kamel, Sourabh Kumar, Daniel Oblak
abstract: Microwave-to-optical quantum transducers are essential for entangling remote superconducting qubits. Among the available transduction platforms, ensembles of Er$^{3+}$ and Yb$^{3+}$ ions doped into solids have emerged as leading candidates. While external magnetic fields are needed to split the Zeeman levels of erbium ions and enable a microwave--qubit interface, superconducting qubits suffer decoherence in such fields. In contrast, ytterbium ions exhibit zero-first-order Zeeman transitions and large hyperfine splittings at zero magnetic field (when doped into inorganic crystals). Owing to its long optical and spin coherence times, Yb:YSO has been widely used as a quantum memory, yet its potential for quantum transduction remains largely unexplored. Investigating this material could enable the integration of quantum memory and transduction in a single platform. Here, we demonstrate microwave-to-optical transduction in the continuous-wave regime using a 5\,ppm doped Yb:YSO crystal. The internal transduction efficiency is $2\times10^{-8}$ with a bandwidth of 200\,kHz, achieved using a 3D loop-gap microwave resonator (LGR) and a single-pass optical configuration. We explore all the ground states that form a V-type three-level system with the first and second optical excited states and assert the use of the ground state, which provides the highest efficiency and isolated optical transition. We further establish strong spin-microwave coupling from avoided crossing measurements. With a strong microwave drive to saturate the spin transition, we estimate the spin population pumped into the excited state, close to the simulated value. Finally, we calculate target parameter values for maximum efficiency with our system and suggest using 50\,ppm doped Yb:YSO crystal. With the calculated target parameters, the internal transduction efficiency is predicted to reach up to $10^{-4}$ in the current LGR.
summary: This paper demonstrates coherent microwave-to-optical quantum transduction using $	ext{Yb}:	ext{YSO}$ spins coupled to a 3D microwave resonator. By leveraging the zero-field properties of $	ext{Yb}^{3+}$, the authors achieve a measurable transduction efficiency, which they predict can be significantly enhanced by increasing the dopant concentration. This work advances the integration of quantum memory and quantum transduction in a single solid-state platform.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical need for efficient microwave-to-optical (M2O) quantum transducers to enable entanglement between remote superconducting qubits.
main_result: The authors demonstrated M2O transduction in Yb:YSO with an initial internal efficiency of $2 	imes 10^{-8}$, while theoretically predicting an improvement up to $10^{-4}$ using higher doping concentrations.
method: The experiment uses continuous-wave (CW) measurements involving a 3D loop-gap microwave resonator (LGR) and single-pass optical coupling to measure the transduction efficiency via the microwave $S_{21}$ parameter.
model_or_system: The system utilizes $	ext{Yb}^{3+}$ ions doped into a $	ext{YSO}$ crystal. $	ext{Yb}^{3+}$ is advantageous because it exhibits zero-first-order Zeeman (ZEFOZ) transitions, allowing operation without external magnetic fields that cause decoherence in superconducting qubits.
key_observables: Internal transduction efficiency ($\eta_{M2O}$), spin-microwave coupling strength ($g_{m,ens}$), and the LGR reflection spectrum ($S_{21}$).
important_parameters: Doping concentration (5 ppm vs. predicted 50 ppm), bandwidth (200 kHz), and the strong cooperativity regime ($	ext{C}_{	ext{m}} > 1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes negligible residual environmental magnetic fields and relies on complex signal processing (noise de-embedding) to isolate the weak transduction signal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level structure, the experimental setup using the LGR, the measured transduction efficiency spectrum, and the avoided crossing measurements showing spin-microwave coupling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical necessity of M2O transducers to detailing the experimental setup, presenting initial measurements of efficiency and coupling strength, and concluding with theoretical scaling predictions for improved performance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines cavity QED principles (strong coupling to a resonator) with solid-state quantum memory platforms ($	ext{Yb}:	ext{YSO}$) to solve a major engineering bottleneck in quantum networking.
